post.description:
Upload a file directly to the datasource system.

This endpoint handles the complete upload process:
1. Validates file type and size (via dependency)
2. Calculates file hash for deduplication
3. Checks if file already exists (returns existing if found)
4. Uploads to S3 if new
5. Creates database record
6. Extracts knowledge to Graphiti graph (for PDFs, if enabled)

Args:
    validated_file: Validated file data (injected by dependency)
    metadata: Optional JSON string for additional metadata
    datasource_service: Injected datasource service
    current_user: Current authenticated user with permissions

Returns:
    Complete datasource details including S3 URL

Sync files from Google Drive to datasources with per-folder real-time monitoring.

This endpoint:
1. Sets up one Watch API channel per folder for real-time synchronization (immediate)
2. Starts background file sync: lists, downloads, and uploads files to S3 (async)

The endpoint returns immediately after setting up watches. File synchronization
continues in the background.

Args:
    sync_request: Request containing folder IDs and recursive flag
    cloud_storage_sync_service: Injected sync service
    token_service: Injected token service
    current_user: Current authenticated user with permissions

Returns:
    Watch setup status (file sync happens in background)

post.description:
Webhook endpoint for Google Drive change notifications.

This endpoint handles real-time notifications from Google Drive Watch API
and synchronizes changes (new files, updated files, deleted files).

Headers:
    X-Goog-Channel-ID: Channel ID from watch setup
    X-Goog-Resource-State: State of the resource (sync, add, remove, update, trash, untrash, change)

Sync files from SharePoint to datasources with per-folder real-time monitoring.

This endpoint:
1. Sets up one Watch API channel per folder for real-time synchronization (immediate)
2. Starts background file sync: lists, downloads, and uploads files to S3 (async)

The endpoint returns immediately after setting up watches. File synchronization
continues in the background.

Args:
    sync_request: Request containing folder IDs and recursive flag
    cloud_storage_sync_service: Injected sync service
    token_service: Injected token service
    current_user: Current authenticated user with permissions

Returns:
    Watch setup status (file sync happens in background)

Webhook endpoint for SharePoint/OneDrive change notifications.

Microsoft Graph sends notifications when files change in monitored folders
and synchronizes changes (new files, updated files, deleted files).

Note: SharePoint subscriptions are created at the root level, but we filter
changes to only process files in the folders specified in the watch record.

Validation:
    When setting up a subscription, Microsoft Graph sends a validation request
    with a validationToken query parameter that must be returned in plain text.

Notification:
    After validation, Microsoft Graph sends POST requests with notification data
    containing the subscription ID and change information.

post.description:
Synchronize Cognito user with local database

This endpoint should be called after user registration in Cognito on the frontend
to ensure the user record exists in the local database for proper authentication
and authorization within the application.

The endpoint creates or updates a user record in the local database based on the
authenticated Cognito user's information (sub, username, email).

x-tenant-id: Tenant ID is not required for this endpoint

Returns:
    GenericResponse: User synchronization result with user details

post.description:
Create a new tenant and grant the user instructor permissions

Creates a new tenant and automatically adds the authenticated user as an instructor
with instructor:tenant:write permissions, allowing them to manage the tenant.

x-tenant-id: Tenant ID is not required for this endpoint

Args:
    request: TenantCreateRequest containing tenant name and description
    
Returns:
    GenericResponse[TenantResponse]: The created tenant details

Accept an invitation using the provided token

Accepts an invitation using the token provided in the email link.
This will add the authenticated user to the specified tenant and grant any permissions
that were included in the invitation.

The user ID is automatically obtained from the authenticated user's token,
ensuring security by preventing token hijacking.

x-tenant-id: Tenant ID is not required for this endpoint

Args:
    request: AcceptInvitationRequest containing only the invitation token
    
Returns:
    GenericResponse[InvitationResponse]: The accepted invitation details
